analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 03 Nov: CCEP (-ve), Hugo Boss (-ve), Zalando (/), ABF (+ve), adidas d/g to sell
key_insights: Nasdaq fell 1.4% and is in correction territory, with futures trading through Friday's lows. The damage was concentrated in the AI complex (Neoclouds -8%, Memory -5%, Momentum -4.7%).
Quality (+2.4%) and Consumer Staples/Discretionary (+1.5-2.5%) continued to absorb flows as the rotational unwind runs its course.
META ($20bn debt) and ORCL ($20bn equity + debt) are both tapping funding markets at a challenged time for sentiment. AAPL fell 3% after hours on a soft services growth guide.

Asia read-through is orderly, with KOSPI/TAIEX down 3-4% and Japan closed. China marginally outperforms after a regulators' support package: a 3rd SFISF operation (>100bn CNY), lower buyback refinancing loan rates and more room on margin financing.

Equities took no comfort from crude finishing down double digits. Iran's president said the Supreme Leader gave the government more authority to negotiate and Trump signalled a deal could come before the midterms, though reports of further strikes continue.

UBS Derivatives Strategy expects Risk Control to turn to buyers after two days of heavy selling, and says CTA supply is largely complete. Retail, foreign investors and multi-asset managers have bought the dip for three sessions.

US midterms: Democrats lead the generic ballot by 8-9pts and are priced at roughly 80-90% to win the House and 60-67% to take the Senate. A blue sweep looks largely priced and should flatten the curve only modestly. A Republican sweep is the bigger risk and could trigger a sharp long-end sell-off.
After the election, Treasury's quarterly refunding keeps risks biased toward higher long-end yields and renewed curve steepening.

Hugo Boss: Q3 organic sales of -5% beat consensus (-7%) and UBSe (-8%), but 2026 guidance was cut on weaker consumer demand assumptions and higher non-cash D&A on IT assets. New EBIT guide of EUR250-300m sits about 11% below consensus at the midpoint.

adidas downgraded to Sell by UBS with PT cut to EUR156 from EUR160. UBS sees 2027 sales growth of +4% vs consensus +7% and 2027-28 EBIT more than 10% below consensus, with industry growth at low-single-digit vs a historical high-single-digit average.

adidas shares are up 20% from the early-October low, which UBS says opens a gap between valuation and the near-term earnings outlook. Gross margin is seen about 100bps below consensus on mix and input costs.

Zalando: Q3 GMV growth of +7.5% and sales growth of +5.1% beat consensus. Adj EBIT of EUR106.5mn was above consensus but within the buyside range of EUR100-110mn. FY26 guidance unchanged, with adj EBIT of EUR680-720m.
Zalando B2B revenue accelerated 28% to EUR354m with adj EBIT margin of 11.9% vs 7.1%. B2C margin pressure from promotions and marketing is a call focus.

ABF: FY26 group adj EBIT of GBP1,508m was in line. Primark adj EBIT margin of 10.2% was modestly ahead of consensus (10.0%). FY27 Grocery outlook was trimmed to broadly in line with FY26, and group EBIT and EPS are expected below FY26 mainly on Sugar. UBS stays Neutral with PT 1980p. Shares remain short crowded.

CCEP: Q3 beat on organic volume (+3.6% vs cons +3.4%) but Europe volume of +2.3% missed Nielsen-based expectations of about +6%, with some German customer disruption in September. FY26 guidance was reiterated rather than narrowed to the top end, which UBS expects to be received poorly.

ABI North America CEO Brendan Whitworth is leaving to become CEO of Equinox with no successor named. Galderma's CFO, in post since May 2026, is stepping down for family and career reasons with no strategic disagreement reported.

Estee Lauder beat on 1Q EPS and raised the FY27 outlook, but UBS stays Neutral, saying the guidance midpoint implies lower estimates for the rest of the year and that re-rating needs sustained organic sales growth. Make-up OSG of 1% was below consensus of 2.9%, a mixed read-across to Intercos.
Newell Brands shares are up 14% since Friday's print. UBS says valuation leaves less room for error and stays Neutral.
Ahead of Q3: UBS expects Warby Parker total sales growth of 10.7% (cons 10.5%) and sees Dillard's with a slightly unfavorable upside/downside skew into the print (Sell).
UBS Softlines quant screen prefers Buy-rated ANF, SIG, ATZ and ONON over Neutral-rated GOOS, OXM, REAL and VFC over the next three months.

China consumption is K-shaped: tighter social-insurance enforcement could pressure mass-market discretionary spending in 2027, while premium, outdoor and experience-led categories look more resilient. Anta reiterated 2026 guidance.

Paris tourism demand is under near-term pressure after the Oct. 17 riots, with bookings down 18% YoY in the following week and luxury hotels seeing a 20% cancellation rate in the last week of October.

EssilorLuxottica: heir Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio proposed buying out his family from Delfin, countering a Czech offer made in October, and plans to present to shareholders on Nov. 7. No terms were given.
Tesco held talks to buy up to 150 Poundland shops, according to press reports citing sources. Tesco declined to comment.

sector_views.rationale: Staples and discretionary absorbed flows (+1.5-2.5%) as the tech rotation unwind ran, but this is a flow description and not a stated UBS stance.
UBS sees industry growth at low-single-digit in 2026 and 2027 vs a historical high-single-digit average.
UBS expects a K-shaped China consumer, with premium categories more resilient than mass-market.

earnings_insights: Hugo Boss Q3 (reported 3 Nov): group organic sales -5% vs VA consensus -7% (UBSe -8%). Gross margin 63.3% vs consensus 62.4%. EBIT margin 8.6% vs consensus 8.7%. FY26 EBIT guide cut to EUR250-300m from EUR300-350m (consensus EUR309m, UBSe EUR300m).

Zalando Q3 (reported 3 Nov): GMV EUR4,536mn vs consensus EUR4,477mn. Sales EUR3,174mn vs consensus EUR3,158mn. Adj EBIT EUR106.5mn vs consensus EUR102mn, buyside bar EUR100-110mn. FY26 adj EBIT guide of EUR680-720m (consensus EUR695m).

CCEP Q3 (reported 3 Nov): organic volume +3.6% vs company-compiled consensus +3.4%. Europe volume +2.3% vs consensus +2.5%. APS volume +6.4% vs consensus +5.0%. Q3 OSG +5.8% vs consensus +4.9%. FY26 guidance reiterated: revenue +3-4%, operating profit about +7%, comparable FCF at least EUR1.7bn.

ABF FY26 results (reported 3 Nov): group adj EBIT GBP1,508m, in line with UBSe and VA consensus. Primark adj EBIT GBP1,005m, about 2% ahead of consensus. Sugar loss GBP47m vs UBSe GBP60m and consensus GBP53m. UBSe FY27 adj group EBIT trimmed by under 1% to GBP1,459m.
Estee Lauder FQ1 27 (reported): EPS beat above both UBSe and Street estimates and FY27 outlook raised. Make-up OSG +1% vs consensus 2.9%. Consensus expects Make-up growth of +2.3% in FY27.

Warby Parker Q3 preview (estimates, not yet reported): UBSe total sales growth 10.7% vs consensus 10.5%, within company guidance of about 10-11%. UBSe retail growth 15.3% vs consensus 13.0%. UBSe eCommerce -2.0% vs consensus +3.5%.
Dillard's Q3 preview (estimate): UBS expects comp sales of +1% y/y, with comps of +1% in 2Q25 vs +3% in 3Q25 as comparison base.

Upcoming earnings feedback and previews: Intercos Q3 (5 Nov), Orkla Q3 (6 Nov), Henkel Q3 (10 Nov), CCH Q3 sales (4 Nov), Diageo Q1 FY27 sales (5 Nov), Pandora Q3 (4 Nov), Burberry H1 (12 Nov), Richemont Q2 (13 Nov), Ferrari Q3 (3 Nov).
ABI NA: Q3 US was weak after a solid H1, per UBS. Newell shares rallied 14% after Friday's print.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Buy-rated ANF, SIG, ATZ and ONON over Neutral-rated GOOS, OXM, REAL and VFC (softlines quant screen)
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS combines fundamental outlooks with factors it thinks should work best: highest daily price fluctuation last 3m, price acceleration last 3m, and lowest net debt to assets.

risk_factors: Further tech and AI-complex selling, with Nasdaq already in correction territory and futures below Friday's lows.
Funding supply from large issuers (META $20bn debt, ORCL $20bn equity + debt) at a challenged time for sentiment.
A Republican sweep in the midterms could prompt a sharp long-end sell-off, and Treasury refunding keeps long-end yields biased higher.
Weak consumer demand and higher non-cash D&A on IT assets, which cut Hugo Boss's 2026 guidance.
A slower 2H organic sales trajectory at Estee Lauder would undermine further re-rating.
Social-insurance enforcement in China could weigh on mass-market consumption in 2027.
Management changes: ABI North America CEO and Galderma CFO are both leaving.
Six fewer consumption days in Q4 and Europe volume trends at CCEP.
vol_and_positioning: UBS Derivatives Strategy estimates Risk Control will turn to buyers after two consecutive days of heavy selling, and CTA supply is largely complete with limited incremental impact from here.
Retail, foreign investors and multi-asset managers have bought the dip over the past three sessions.

European flow on Monday finished balanced (51/49) with participation about 40% above the HT YTD average. Banks were 19% of turnover and finished better for sale, healthcare was 18% with strong pharma demand.
ABF shares are up 7% over one month into the print but remain short crowded on UBS data.
Most crowded softlines longs are TJX, ROST and VFC. Most crowded softlines shorts are LULU, CROX and DBI.
Dillard's shares have historically moved +/-7.9% around earnings, though UBS expects volatility below that.
geopolitical: Iran: President Pezeshkian said the Supreme Leader granted additional authority to pursue negotiations, Trump signalled a deal could be struck ahead of the midterms, and reports of further strikes continue.
US midterm elections begin today with first results after East Coast polls close Tuesday evening. Last poll to close is Alaska at 06:00 GMT Wednesday 4 Nov.
China regulators announced a support package: a 3rd SFISF operation (>100bn CNY), cuts to buyback refinancing loan rates and more room on margin financing.
Middle East geopolitical volatility weighed on store traffic and Hugo Boss's sales in the region.
Paris riots on Oct. 17 caused a drop in tourist bookings and hotel cancellations.

tension_points.bull_case: A blue sweep looks largely priced, with Democrats at roughly 80-90% to win the House, and should produce only modest curve flattening.
tension_points.bear_case: A Republican sweep could prompt a sharp long-end sell-off, and Treasury's quarterly refunding keeps risks biased toward higher long-end yields and curve steepening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Republican sweep in the midterm results, with first unofficial results due Tuesday evening and the last poll closing 06:00 GMT Wednesday 4 Nov.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong execution around the World Cup and a compelling apparel offering supported double-digit sales growth in 2026, and shares have recovered 20% from the early-October low.
tension_points.bear_case: UBS sees industry growth at low-single-digit, +4% 2027 sales vs consensus +7%, gross margin about 100bps below consensus and 2027-28 EBIT more than 10% below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful acceleration in footwear and lifestyle, which UBS says it does not see today.

tension_points.bull_case: EPS beat, raised FY27 outlook and broad-based top-line strength, with UBS saying the business is on better footing and FY27 EPS guidance looks more than achievable.
tension_points.bear_case: The guidance midpoint implies estimates for the rest of the year must move lower, and UBS struggles to see a re-rating if organic sales growth slows in the 2H.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Organic sales growth slowing in the 2H, which is the assumption embedded in guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 beat on organic volume and OSG, and FY26 guidance was reiterated with a company statement that the business remains resilient.
tension_points.bear_case: Europe volume of +2.3% fell short of Nielsen-implied +6% expectations, and guidance was not narrowed toward the top end as expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Conference call evidence on Europe volume trends and Q4 pricing/mix, with six fewer consumption days in Q4.
